characters.name: Anselm Voss-Rietveld
characters.line: I could brief Capital myself. They remember me from training.

characters.name: Pavel Oskarsen
characters.line: I have seen six ambassadors. Five also thought a promise was a reservation.

characters.name: Sola Dewrin
characters.line: I can make the calls. But I am not everybody’s translator and emergency exit.

characters.name: Elise
characters.line: The Minister could visit our project. Provided we remember the people, not just the photograph.

characters.name: Bianca Montefiore
characters.line: A convoy needs vehicles, not a beautifully formatted spreadsheet.

characters.name: Ines Thibault-Lund
characters.line: Four hundred people in the queue. No, they do not disappear when the Minister arrives.

characters.name: Lucien Falk
characters.line: A good photograph is worth a thousand words. Legal would prefer zero.

characters.name: Maxim
characters.line: I made a checklist of the checklists. Is that useful?

characters.name: Ketu Marrimba
characters.line: I can feed the delegation. I cannot feed its ego.

characters.name: Director Ndao
characters.line: Permission has three stamps. You have submitted two and a coffee stain.

characters.name: Celeste Norren
characters.line: Yes, Bellaluxe contributes 17.6% of the EU's Multiannual Financial Framework. No, that is not your biscuit quota.

characters.name: Marcel Deux
characters.line: Everything is possible. The question is who owes whom afterwards.

characters.name: Ruth Vale
characters.line: Off the record is an agreement, not something you say after the quote.

characters.name: Minister Bako
characters.line: An appointment? My secretary says I am unavailable. My caddie disagrees.

characters.name: Dr Amara Chen
characters.line: We can support the programme. We cannot promise six agencies will agree on one logo.

characters.name: Ambassador Mara Velen
characters.line: My national-day speech was eight minutes. The applause was longer because the exit was locked.

characters.name: Ambassador Niko Arden
characters.line: Denmark supports consensus, provided someone else writes the first draft.

characters.name: Mira Sene
characters.line: The port needs a working waste collection, not another photograph of an empty bin.

characters.name: Sofia da Costa
characters.line: I can introduce you to the insurers. First tell me who actually maintains the harbour.

characters.name: Idra Venn
characters.line: The donor reports say the bins have arrived. The bins say they are still in customs.

characters.name: Klaus Weber
characters.line: The coordination table is in Annex IV. The chairs have their own annex.

characters.name: Henri de Valois
characters.line: The draft is acceptable in principle. In French, the principle is considerably more elegant.

characters.name: Tanya Farrugia
characters.line: I have Malta's brief and, with permission for this meeting, the briefs from Cyprus and Luxembourg. They agree on the biscuits, at least.

characters.name: Lars Lindqvist
characters.line: Before we decide who speaks, perhaps we should ask who has not been invited.

venues.name: Embassy kitchen
venues.description: Staff coffee and a lunch assembled by Ketu.

venues.name: Chez Marcel
venues.description: Classic French and Italian dining. Quiet tables, serious cutlery.

venues.name: Auntie’s Courtyard
venues.description: Local cuisine, open-air tables and conversations that travel.

venues.name: The Gilded Palm
venues.description: Rooftop chandeliers, imported everything, a very visible bill.

venues.name: Mizu
venues.description: Sushi, minimalist surroundings and ambitious small plates.

venues.name: The Quiet Amendment
venues.description: A discreet bar with food and excessively well-informed regulars.

locations.name: Embassy
locations.description: Your team, your in-tray, your responsibility.

locations.name: Foreign Ministry / Protocol
locations.description: Appointments, landing permissions and wounded precedence.

locations.name: EU Delegation
locations.description: Coordination, contested clauses and exactly 17.6% of the refreshments.

locations.name: The Quiet Amendment
locations.description: Rumours and favours that never quite stay unofficial.

locations.name: Press Correspondents Club
locations.description: Access, credibility and the dangerous phrase “off the record”.

locations.name: Precedence Golf Club
locations.description: The people who never answer letters are available on the ninth green.

locations.name: UN House & multilateral circuit
locations.description: Programmes, funding, mandates and competing logos.

opening.text: {line} What do you want to discuss?

choices.label: How are things going, really?
What would help you do your job?
Capital expects results. No excuses.

listen.text: People will work with you if you notice what it costs them. Public credit would be a start.

choices.label: You will get the credit. I’ll back you publicly.
choices.result: Your promise of public credit makes the team more willing to share information.

choices.label: Let’s keep personal feelings out of this.
choices.result: The conversation ends politely. Cooperation becomes rather less enthusiastic.

support.text: A clear brief, realistic time and no surprise overtime. Can you manage that?

choices.label: Agreed. We’ll protect your time.
choices.result: Clear boundaries earn trust and reduce friction with the rest of the team.

choices.label: Help now; I’ll owe you a favour.
choices.result: A favour is accepted. It will not be forgotten.

pressure.text: You can order compliance. You cannot order enthusiasm. Is that what you want?

choices.label: Fair point. Let’s agree priorities.
choices.result: You step back from the threat and agree workable priorities.

choices.label: Yes. Have it ready, or explain yourself to HQ.
choices.result: The instruction is accepted. Trust and cooperation suffer.

events.title: The 17.6% meeting
events.text: Celeste calls the local EU coordination meeting to order. Bellaluxe contributes 17.6% of the EU's Multiannual Financial Framework; your colleague has brought a stopwatch to claim 17.6% of the speaking time, biscuits and credit. Tanya of Malta says Cyprus and Luxembourg have authorised her to present their briefs at this meeting. France wants to reach the host ministry before it closes. Germany has already put the stopwatch in an annex.

choices.label: Claim Bellaluxe's 17.6% of speaking time and biscuits
choices.result: Your colleague starts the stopwatch. Tanya's Cyprus and Luxembourg briefs are postponed until after the biscuits. Capital appreciates the visible arithmetic.

choices.label: Give Tanya time to present Malta's, Cyprus's and Luxembourg's views
choices.result: Tanya presents all three briefs. Celeste calls it Team Europe; the stopwatch records 17.6% of a very patient silence.

choices.label: Propose equal initial speaking time, then discuss the budget
choices.result: Klaus agrees to an equal first round, subject to a one-page annex. Henri gets to the ministry before it closes.

choices.label: Propose a toast to the budget share
choices.result: Celeste agrees to a toast; the stopwatch is temporarily repurposed as a coaster.

events.title: The missing Cyprus paragraph
events.text: Tanya calls: Cyprus's authorised position was left out after Bellaluxe's stopwatch expired. The statement is still a draft, but the biscuits are not.

choices.label: Ask Celeste to add the Cyprus paragraph
choices.result: Tanya supplies the authorised paragraph and Celeste amends the draft. Capital asks whether the correction used any of its speaking time.

choices.label: Leave the draft as it is
choices.result: The draft goes forward without Cyprus's paragraph. Tanya promises to bring a larger stopwatch.

events.title: Two briefs and a cup of coffee
events.text: Tanya thanks you for giving Malta, Cyprus and Luxembourg time to speak. Cyprus has now authorised a concise amendment; the host's protocol desk says it can accept it before lunch.

choices.label: Support the authorised amendment
choices.result: The amendment reaches the host desk. Both missions receive credit; Celeste asks whether the cover page can say Team Europe.

choices.label: Defer it until Bellaluxe has checked with Capital
choices.result: Capital receives the amendment for review. Tanya points out that lunch was the deadline, not a suggestion.

events.title: The annex on equal time
events.text: Klaus has reduced the equal-time proposal to one page, plus an annex defining a page. Celeste asks whether Bellaluxe will endorse the rule before the next meeting.

choices.label: Endorse the equal first round
choices.result: Klaus circulates the rule. Everyone gets a turn to object to the annex.

choices.label: Request a 17.6% exception for Bellaluxe
choices.result: Klaus adds a second annex titled 'exception to equal time'. Capital asks for a copy.

events.title: Team Europe and the clean port
events.text: Celeste proposes a Team Europe clean-port initiative: member states supply money and staff, while her draft announcement credits the EU Delegation. Ombrazia's port environment officer Mira Sene says collection routes and local crews matter more than a launch photograph. Germany's Klaus has offered safety advice; Bellaluxe must decide whether to contribute.

choices.label: Accept the Delegation-led announcement; fund collection planning
choices.result: Elise and local crews plan collection; Bellaluxe pays ƒ200. Celeste announces the Delegation initiative. Capital asks where Bellaluxe appears.

choices.label: Insist on Bellaluxe branding before contributing
choices.result: Elise prepares a ƒ100 Bellaluxe proposal. Celeste delays the joint announcement; Mira must wait for agreement before scheduling crews.

choices.label: Negotiate shared credit and a practical work plan
choices.result: Elise commits ƒ150 and agrees routes with Mira. The announcement names both Bellaluxe and the Delegation; Celeste wanted the larger logo and Capital wanted the first line.

choices.label: Decline the contribution and keep embassy resources free
choices.result: Bellaluxe keeps its funds and staff time. Celeste seeks another partner, and Mira has no Bellaluxe commitment to schedule.

events.title: The port without a name
events.text: Mira says the collection routes are ready, but the Delegation announcement does not name Bellaluxe. Local crews know Elise did the work; Capital knows only what appeared in the fax.

choices.label: Request a factual correction naming all contributors
choices.result: Mira sends a corrected list of contributors. Celeste says a list can still have a Team Europe heading.

choices.label: Keep the announcement and start collection
choices.result: The crews start work without revising the announcement. Capital files a small but very legible complaint.

events.title: A plaque before a route
events.text: Mira has a Bellaluxe proposal but no agreed joint collection timetable. The Delegation wants the logo question settled; the port wants the rubbish removed.

choices.label: Release the plan for the local crews to use
choices.result: Mira puts the plan to work while the logos remain under discussion. Bellaluxe keeps a named role.

choices.label: Hold the plan until the branding is agreed
choices.result: Capital welcomes the firm position. Mira postpones the crews and asks who will pay for another week of storage.

events.title: Two logos, one collection route
events.text: Mira has scheduled the local crews using Elise’s shared plan. Both Bellaluxe and the Delegation are named, but the announcement leaves out the port workers.

choices.label: Add the port crews to the public credit
choices.result: Mira adds the crews and the collection begins. The revised credit line is longer than the route description.

choices.label: Publish the agreed version on time
choices.result: The announcement appears on schedule. The crews start work, but Mira notes whose names were omitted.

events.title: The missing port partner
events.text: Mira says Celeste is looking for another contributor. Without a Bellaluxe commitment, the port is adjusting the schedule rather than counting on work that was never promised.

choices.label: Offer Mira an introduction without promising funds or staff
choices.result: Mira receives a useful contact; the port still needs a funded partner before expanding collection.

choices.label: Wait for the Delegation to find a partner
choices.result: Mira adjusts the port timetable. Bellaluxe makes no further commitment.

events.title: Whose project is it?
events.text: Sola has been asked to translate Elise's finished project proposal for local partners. Elise is proud of her work; Sola says the partners should have been asked what they need before the proposal was written. The visit team wants a decision today.

choices.label: Ask Sola and the partners to shape the proposal with Elise
choices.result: Sola contacts the partners before the proposal is finalised. Elise agrees to revise it, although her timetable is now rather less beautiful.

choices.label: Tell Sola to translate Elise’s proposal as written
choices.result: Sola translates the proposal. Elise meets her deadline, but the partners have not yet been asked what they need.

choices.label: Pause the proposal until both colleagues can agree a process
choices.result: Sola and Elise agree to discuss the process. The proposal waits; neither has promised an immediate answer.

events.title: A project with local authors
events.text: Elise brings back Sola's notes from the partners. Their priorities differ from her draft, and changing it will mean telling Capital the original proposal was incomplete.

choices.label: Back the partners’ revisions and explain them to Capital
choices.result: Elise and Sola name the partners as contributors. Capital receives a revised proposal and a less flattering timeline.

choices.label: Keep the original draft but acknowledge the consultation
choices.result: The draft leaves on time. Sola points out that acknowledgement is not the same as using the partners’ advice.

events.title: The translation comes back
events.text: The local partners have returned the translated proposal with practical objections. Sola says she would have raised these earlier if anyone had asked. Elise wants a chance to put them right.

choices.label: Acknowledge the mistake and ask Sola and Elise to revise it
choices.result: Sola accepts the apology and arranges a revision with Elise. The delay is real; so is the improvement.

choices.label: Send the original proposal and note the objections separately
choices.result: Capital gets the proposal on time. Sola sends the partners a separate explanation of why their comments were not included.

events.title: A process, eventually
events.text: Elise and Sola have agreed to ask the partners for comments, but neither wants to own the delayed deadline. Capital has noticed the blank in the timetable.

choices.label: Take responsibility for the delay and agree a new deadline
choices.result: You take the call from Capital. Sola and Elise agree who will consult the partners and when.

choices.label: Tell Capital the two colleagues are responsible
choices.result: Capital gets two names. Elise and Sola get a reason to be wary of their next joint brief.

events.title: The joint briefing returns
events.text: Anselm has incorporated Pavel’s corrections and asks whether his contribution will be named, as you promised when mediating their dispute. Pavel wants the facts checked before the briefing goes to Capital.

choices.label: Check the facts and credit both authors
choices.result: The briefing names both authors. Pavel checks the figures; Anselm discovers that an edit is not an accusation.

choices.label: Send it under your own name to save time
choices.result: Capital gets the briefing. Anselm and Pavel compare notes about your interpretation of shared credit.

events.title: A briefing, reluctantly
events.text: Pavel has sent the combined briefing you ordered. Anselm has written a separate correction and neither will speak to the other. Capital wants one reliable version.

choices.label: Hear both colleagues and agree who checks the facts
choices.result: Pavel and Anselm agree on a fact check. The repair takes time, and neither calls it a friendship.

choices.label: Send Pavel’s version and tell Anselm to drop it
choices.result: Pavel’s version goes to Capital. Anselm files his correction and starts keeping a careful record of whose name is on which draft.

events.title: Your presence is requested immediately
events.text: The host ministry unveils a plaque in twenty minutes. Your absence would be noticed. Your schedule is not their concern.

choices.label: Attend personally — replace your planned activity
choices.result: You attend the ceremony. Your planned work must wait.

choices.label: Send Anselm with a strict brief
choices.result: Anselm represents the mission. The strict brief limits his promises.

choices.label: Decline diplomatically
choices.result: Protocol records your absence with considerable courtesy.

choices.label: Reply to the entire guest list
choices.result: Protocol gets your answer, along with every guest and a confused caterer.

events.title: Two briefings, no shared facts
events.text: Pavel and Anselm each wrote a briefing and refuse to combine them. The Minister cannot hold two contradictory positions.

choices.label: Give Pavel the lead and Anselm visible credit
choices.result: A clear lead and shared credit begin repairing the Pavel–Anselm feud.

choices.label: Order them to cooperate
choices.result: One document appears. They stop speaking to each other.

choices.label: Invoke a former minister to settle authorship
choices.result: Pavel and Anselm accept the former minister as an unlikely authority on their briefing.

events.title: The generous supplier · part I
events.text: A caterer offers an unusually cheap reception. Sola recognises the surname. Investigate or take the bargain?

choices.label: Ask Sola to check the ownership
choices.result: Sola traces the supplier. Marcel at the Quiet Amendment can explain the connection starting Day 2.

choices.label: Accept the offer without questions
choices.result: The bargain is accepted. Marcel at the Quiet Amendment has questions about its strings starting Day 2.

events.title: The generous supplier · part II
events.text: Marcel slides Sola's findings across the table. The supplier belongs to a protocol official’s cousin. A correspondent is asking about the reception. 'I know a different caterer,' he adds. 'And, regrettably, the cousin.'

choices.label: Disclose the connection and change supplier
choices.result: Transparent procurement costs more but prevents a scandal.

choices.label: Keep the deal quiet
choices.result: The cousin is delighted. Capital is less amused by the eventual questions.

events.title: The generous supplier · invoice enclosed
events.text: The caterer's generous price was for plates. The invoice charges separately for food, chairs and the privilege of sitting on them. A protocol official's cousin owns the company.

choices.label: Tell Capital and renegotiate in public
choices.result: Capital admires your transparency after asking why the chairs cost extra.

choices.label: Pay quietly and keep the reception
choices.result: The chairs arrive. So does an invoice for sitting on them twice.

events.title: A chair of national importance
events.text: Director Ndao calls: the draft visit plan seats Ombrazia's Deputy Minister behind a decorative fern. The fern is not accredited. How will you respond?

choices.label: Apologise and ask Protocol to help revise the plan
choices.result: Ndao accepts the apology and invites you to review the seating plan at the Foreign Ministry from Day 4.

choices.label: Defend Capital's seating instructions
choices.result: Ndao requests your presence at the Foreign Ministry from Day 4, with the seating plan and a larger fern.

events.title: The seating plan · a delicate compromise
events.text: Ndao lays out two cards and the disputed fern. A compromise would move the Deputy Minister forward, though Capital's delegation would lose its preferred photograph.

choices.label: Move the Deputy Minister forward and explain to Capital
choices.result: Ndao approves the revised seating plan. Capital asks whether the fern can be photoshopped back in.

choices.label: Keep Capital's original plan
choices.result: Ndao restores the original plan, carefully placing the fern where it can witness the consequences.

events.title: The seating plan · instructions versus chairs
events.text: Ndao has compared Capital's seating instructions with the host's protocol rules. The documents disagree on precedence, furniture and the definition of a doorway.

choices.label: Accept Ndao's compromise and brief Capital
choices.result: A compromise emerges. Both ministries describe it as their original idea.

choices.label: Insist on Capital's instructions
choices.result: Ndao signs the plan with a pen that seems to be under considerable pressure.

events.title: A project, not a photo opportunity
events.text: Elise wants the Minister to meet project beneficiaries, not merely unveil a donor plaque. UN partners demand their own speaking slots.

choices.label: Protect time for beneficiaries
choices.result: Elise asks the UN partners to reserve time for beneficiaries. From Day 3, Amara can discuss the programme at UN House.

choices.label: Prioritise the Minister’s photograph
choices.result: The photograph is secured provisionally. From Day 3, Amara wants to discuss what the visit will actually include at UN House.

events.title: The project visit · whose voices?
events.text: Amara has reserved a project visit with people who use its services. One partner wants to fill the discussion with speeches; the community asks for time to speak for itself.

choices.label: Protect time for the community's questions
choices.result: Amara revises the programme so the community can speak. The speeches are shortened under protest.

choices.label: Give the partners their speaking slots
choices.result: Every partner receives a speaking slot. The community is allotted a photograph.

events.title: The project visit · a perfect photograph
events.text: Amara shows you the proposed photo stop. The camera position is immaculate, but the project team has been given no time to explain what it actually does.

choices.label: Add time for the project team and community
choices.result: Amara makes space for a real discussion. Capital asks if the camera can listen as well.

choices.label: Keep the photograph and official speeches
choices.result: The photograph is perfectly framed. The project team waits politely just outside it.

events.title: The 17.6% entitlement
events.text: Celeste slides the biscuit plate towards you. 'Bellaluxe contributes 17.6% of the EU's Multiannual Financial Framework,' she says. 'That does not make 17.6% of the biscuits, the speaking time, or the minutes of the meeting your national allocation.' The room braces itself.

choices.label: “Naturally. And 17.6% of the talking time, coffee and credit.”
choices.result: Pained expressions all round. Your self-deprecation briefly softens the coalition.

choices.label: Save the joke and discuss the clause
choices.result: The room agrees on the clause. Nobody misses the joke quite enough to admit it.

events.title: The coffee clause · a Danish proposal
events.text: After your conversation over coffee, Ambassador Arden offers Bellaluxe a chance to shape the EU's joint statement. The draft is short; the footnotes are not.

choices.label: Help Niko find a practical compromise
choices.result: Niko includes your amendment. The footnote shrinks by a historic three lines.

choices.label: Claim the proposal as Bellaluxe's initiative
choices.result: Capital is pleased to see Bellaluxe's name. Niko quietly changes the order of the flags.

events.title: The coffee clause · a colleague's introduction
events.text: The colleague you sent made a good impression. Ambassador Arden now offers Bellaluxe a chance to shape the EU's joint statement in person.

choices.label: Help Niko find a practical compromise
choices.result: Niko includes your amendment. The footnote shrinks by a historic three lines.

choices.label: Claim the proposal as Bellaluxe's initiative
choices.result: Capital is pleased to see Bellaluxe's name. Niko quietly changes the order of the flags.

events.title: Off the record · a careful briefing
events.text: Ruth kept your distinction between confirmed and pending arrangements. Now she wants background on the visit. 'You can say no,' she says, which makes you more suspicious.

choices.label: Offer context without naming sources
choices.result: Ruth checks her notes. The background may make a better story than the rumour.

choices.label: Stick to the public line
choices.result: Ruth writes down your public line and draws a small question mark beside it.

events.title: Off the record · the printed promise
events.text: Ruth places your promise that everything is ready beside a list of arrangements that are not. The microphone is conspicuously switched on this time.

choices.label: Correct the claim and explain the work ahead
choices.result: The correction is less glamorous than the promise. It is also considerably more accurate.

choices.label: Insist the arrangements are entirely under control
choices.result: Ruth underlines 'entirely'. The second underline is audible.

events.title: A casual quote
events.text: Ruth asks whether the Minister’s visit is really confirmed. The microphone looks switched off. It is not.

choices.label: Explain what is confirmed and what is pending
choices.result: Your careful distinction survives the headline. From Day 2, Ruth offers a longer conversation at the Press Correspondents Club.

choices.label: Everything is entirely ready
choices.result: The claim is printed. From Day 2, Ruth wants an explanation at the Press Correspondents Club.
